**Diagnosis:** The `C-RET` (Ctrl+Enter) binding is correctly configured for both `vi_imap` (insert mode) and `vi_nmap` (normal mode) to use `accept-line`. The tmux config correctly uses `extended-keys on` (not `always`), which ensures Ctrl+Enter transmits as a CSI-u sequence while preserving legacy encodings for other keys. 

**Why it might not work:**
- Terminal may not support CSI-u encoding (check: `echo $TERM` in tmux)
- tmux needs to be reloaded: `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf`
- ble.sh may not have re-attached after config changes
- Buffer may not actually contain newlines (test: paste multi-line text, then Ctrl+Enter)

  - Lines 47-50: `C-RET` and `M-RET` for accept-line (vi_imap/vi_nmap)

**Diagnosis:** The `:q` prompt on Ctrl+C in vi insert mode is ble.sh's **default behavior**, not something configured in your dotfiles. This is a ble.sh library choice, not a custom keybinding conflict.

254	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
255	
256	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
257	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
258	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
259	
260	# =============================================================================
261	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
262	# =============================================================================
263	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
264	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
265	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
266	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
267	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
268	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
269	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
270	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
271	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
272	#
273	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
274	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
275	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
276	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
277	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
278	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
279	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
280	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
281	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
282	
283	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
284	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
285	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
286	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
287	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
288	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
289	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
290	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
291	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
292	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
293	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
294	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
295	
296	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
297	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
298	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
299	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
300	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
301	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
302	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
303	
304	# =============================================================================
305	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
306	# =============================================================================
307	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
308	
309	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
310	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
311	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
312	
313	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
314	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
315	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
316	
317	# =============================================================================
318	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
319	# =============================================================================
320	
321	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
322	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
323	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
324	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
325	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
326	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
327	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
328	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
329	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
330	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
331	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
332	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
333	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
334	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
335	)\""
336	
337	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
338	
339	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
340	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
341	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
342	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
343	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
344	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see
345	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
346	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
347	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
348	
349	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
350	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
351	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
352	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
353	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
354	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
355	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
356	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
357	
358	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
359	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
360	
361	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
362	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
363	
364	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
365	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
366	
367	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
368	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
369	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
370	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
371	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
372	
373	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
374	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
375	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
376	
377	# =============================================================================
378	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
379	# =============================================================================
380	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
381	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
382	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
383	# the layout" workflows.
384	
385	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
386	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
387	
388	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
389	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
390	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
391	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
392	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
393	
394	# =============================================================================
395	# Help / cheatsheet
396	# =============================================================================
397	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
398	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
399	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
400	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
401	#
402	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
403	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
404	#
405	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
406	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
407	
408	unbind-key '?'
409	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
410	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
411	
412	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
413	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
414	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
415	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
416	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
417	
418	# =============================================================================
419	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
420	# =============================================================================
421	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
422	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
423	#
424	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
425	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
426	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
427	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
428	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
429	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
430	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
431	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
432	#
433	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
434	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
435	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
436	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
437	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
438	#
439	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
440	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
441	# right-click on a pane / status line.
442	
443	unbind-key Space
444	unbind-key Enter
445	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
446	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
447	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
448	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
449	# in the window right-click menu).

2	#
3	# Init order (load-bearing — see docs/shells/bash.md):
4	#   1.  Early-return guard (non-interactive shells)
5	#   2.  /etc/bashrc source (RHEL families)
6	#   3.  ble.sh --attach=none   ← BEFORE bash-preexec / starship
7	#   4.  XDG dirs + Homebrew shellenv (mac)
8	#   5.  Bash-specific config files (history / completion / vi-mode / aliases)
9	#   6.  oh-my-bash source (after ble.sh so OMB's bash-preexec install no-ops)
10	#   7.  Shared modular layer (starship / mise / zoxide / direnv / thefuck)
11	#   8.  atuin init bash --disable-up-arrow (ble.sh handles up-arrow history)
12	#   9.  Secrets
13	#   10. ble-attach   ← absorbs all precmd/preexec stacks accumulated above
14	#   11. ~/.bash_aliases (Debian/Ubuntu) + ~/.bashrc.d/* (RHEL family)
15	#       — backward-compat with distro skel conventions
16	#   12. .bashrc.adhoc tail (chezmoi-ignored; highest-priority user override)
17	#
18	# The ble.sh / oh-my-bash / atuin steps are presence-gated and no-op
19	# silently when the artefact isn't installed (e.g. fresh host before
20	# `chezmoi apply` finishes the externals + run-onchange-after_install).
21	# Plain bash without ble.sh + OMB still gets a fully working starship
22	# prompt + the shared layer + bash-completion v2.
23	
24	# 1. ============================================================
25	# Non-interactive shells (SSH commands, cron, scp) bail out here.
26	# Anything below this guard runs only in interactive bash.
27	# Mirrors /etc/skel/.bashrc convention on Debian/Ubuntu.
28	case $- in
29	    *i*) ;;
30	      *) return ;;
31	esac
32	
33	# 2. ============================================================
34	# /etc/bashrc on RHEL families carries the protective `rm -i`
35	# aliases, the Modules system init, and umask defaults. Source it
36	# first so we don't lose those — and so anything we set below can
37	# override (we set HISTSIZE etc. larger than RHEL's defaults).
38	# Debian/Ubuntu has no /etc/bashrc, so this is a no-op there.
39	[ -r /etc/bashrc ] && . /etc/bashrc
40	
41	# 3. ============================================================
42	# ble.sh --attach=none lets us chain starship/atuin between this
43	# point and `ble-attach` at the end. Sourcing ble.sh AFTER
44	# bash-preexec (which starship installs) is the #1 ble.sh footgun
45	# documented at https://github.com/akinomyoga/ble.sh/wiki/
46	# So we source it FIRST, with --attach=none, then call ble-attach
47	# only at the very end. Presence-gated for hosts where
48	# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_NN_install_blesh.sh

51	    # shellcheck disable=SC1091

57	export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}"
58	export XDG_DATA_HOME="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}"

66	# $HOMEBREW_PREFIX detection works.
67	if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
68	    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
69	elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
70	    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
71	fi

76	# shares the same name + signature). Globs $dir/*.<ext> and sources
77	# each file in alphabetical order.
78	load_modular_dir() {
79	    local dir="$1"
80	    local ext="${2:-bash}"

82	    local _had_nullglob; _had_nullglob=$(shopt -p nullglob)

86	        [[ -r "$f" ]] && source "$f"

91	# Bash-specific config (history / completion / vi-mode / aliases).
92	# Loaded BEFORE oh-my-bash so ~/.config/bash/01_omb_plugins.bash can
93	# set the `plugins=()` array that oh-my-bash.sh then consumes.

97	# oh-my-bash. Theme MUST be empty so starship owns the prompt.
98	# OMB's autosuggestions / syntax-highlighting / history-substring-search
99	# plugins are excluded in dot_config/bash/01_omb_plugins.bash because
100	# ble.sh provides better native versions.

110	# Shared POSIX layer — env vars (PATH, GFW mirrors, GOPATH, BUN_INSTALL,
111	# PNPM_HOME), tool init wrappers (starship/mise/zoxide/direnv/thefuck),

117	# atuin (history sync) — `--disable-up-arrow` is mandatory when
118	# ble.sh is loaded; ble.sh's history navigation owns the up arrow.

130	# registered their precmd / preexec hooks, hand control over to ble.sh.

132	if [[ -n $BLE_VERSION ]]; then

137	# Backward-compat with distro-specific user-customisation conventions:
138	#
139	#   - ~/.bash_aliases               (Ubuntu/Debian skel sources this)
140	#   - ~/.bashrc.d/*                 (RHEL/Rocky/Alma/Fedora skel loops
141	#                                    over this dir — verified in Rocky 9)
142	#
143	# Without these sources, our managed bashrc would silently strip user
144	# content that other dotfiles / distro defaults accumulated — hard to
145	# debug, hostile UX.
146	#

14	# Hide the message ble.sh prints on attach (attach-greeting), keeps shell
15	# startup quiet.
16	bleopt prompt_eol_mark=
17	
18	# Vi-mode keymap: ble.sh auto-detects `set -o vi` (set in 05_vi_mode.bash)
19	# and activates its full vi-mode. No additional config needed.
20	
21	# Custom keybindings — currently none. Drop ble-bind invocations here
22	# (e.g., `ble-bind -x 'C-r' 'atuin-search-bash'`) when porting zsh
23	# widgets to bash; reminder: anything that was `bindkey -M viins` in zsh
24	# is `ble-bind -m vi_imap -x` in ble.sh.
25	
26	# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter ===
27	#
28	# Default ble.sh + vi-mode behaviour: when the buffer contains a newline
29	# (multi-line paste, multi-line typed input, here-doc etc.), the shell
30	# enters MULTILINE mode and plain RET / Ctrl-M re-binds to "insert
31	# newline" rather than "submit" — meaning Enter alone won't run the
32	# command. The official escape is Ctrl-J (linefeed = accept-line), but
33	# tmux's vim-tmux-navigator already eats `C-j` for pane navigation
34	# (dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:183), so it never reaches ble.sh.
35	#
36	# Ctrl+Enter is the cleanest free key on this stack:
37	#   - tmux extended-keys + xterm:extkeys are enabled, so Ctrl+Enter
38	#     sends a distinct CSI-u sequence (\e[13;5u) which tmux forwards
39	#     intact (no collision with C-j).
40	#   - ble.sh sees `C-RET` as a separate keysym when extended-keys flow
41	#     through, and binds it independently from `RET` / `C-m`.
42	#   - Plain RET still does the safe-multiline-newline thing — useful for
43	#     intentionally building multi-line commands.
44	#
45	# If your terminal can't emit Ctrl+Enter as CSI-u (some minimal SSH
46	# clients), Alt+Enter (`M-RET` below) is a portable fallback.
47	ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
48	ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
49	ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
50	ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
51	
52	# === Suppress mouse keyseq warnings ===
53	#
54	# When ble.sh runs OUTSIDE tmux (e.g. directly in Ghostty / Alacritty), the
55	# terminal forwards mouse-tracking sequences (`ESC[<...M`) into the shell.
56	# ble.sh by default doesn't have a binding for them and warns
57	# `unbind keyseq: mouse` on every mouse click, which cluters the prompt.
58	# Inside tmux mouse events stay in tmux's own copy-mode handler, so the
59	# warning never appears.
60	#
61	# Bind every mouse keyseq variant to `nop` (no-op) — ble.sh swallows the
62	# event silently. Both `xterm` (modern SGR-style) and the legacy `mouse`
63	# pseudo-keysym are covered.
64	ble-bind -f 'mouse' nop 2>/dev/null
65	ble-bind -f 'mouse_xterm' nop 2>/dev/null
66

## ble.sh Issues: Debugging Report

I've thoroughly analyzed your ble.sh installation (version 0.4.0-devel4+b99cadb) and found answers to both issues.

### Issue 1: C-RET in Multiline Mode

**The problem:** `C-RET` is bound to `accept-line` in both `vi_imap` and `vi_nmap`, but when there are newlines in the buffer (multiline mode), it doesn't submit.

**Root cause:** This is **expected behavior by design**. When ble.sh detects multiple lines in the buffer (via `ble-edit/content/is-single-line` check), it uses a different widget dispatch:

- In **vi_imap**: RET/C-m is bound to `accept-single-line-or-newline` (which inserts a newline if multiline is detected)
- In **vi_nmap**: RET/C-m is bound to `accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space`

Your current bindings at `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash:47-48`:
```bash
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
```

are using the raw `accept-line` widget which **bypasses the multiline check**. The problem is that you're **not using the `accept-single-line-or` wrapper** that checks if the buffer is multiline first.

**Solution for Issue 1:**
Replace your bindings with the properly conditional version:

```bash
# vi_imap: Use accept-single-line-or-newline for intelligent newline/submit behavior
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'

# vi_nmap: Use accept-single-line-or wrapper for intelligent behavior
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'
```

Alternatively, if you want C-RET to **always submit** (even in multiline mode), keep your current `accept-line` binding, but understand this means RET will only insert newlines and C-RET will always submit. The current default behavior in vi_imap is:
- RET = smart (insert newline in multiline, submit if complete)
- C-j = always submit (hardcoded in lines 6354-6355 of keymap.vi.sh)

**Key insight:** There is NO separate `multiline_imap` or `multiline_nmap` keymap. ble.sh uses conditional widget dispatch (`accept-single-line-or` wrapper) instead of separate keymaps to handle multiline detection.

---

### Issue 2: C-c in Vi Normal Mode Shows `:q` Instead of Clearing Buffer

**Current behavior:** When you press Ctrl+C in vi insert mode, it correctly exits to normal mode. But in normal mode, Ctrl+C shows a `:q` prompt instead of clearing the buffer like non-vi mode does.

**Root cause:** The binding at line 4754 of `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/blesh/lib/keymap.vi.sh`:
```bash
ble-bind -f 'C-c' vi-command/cancel
```

The `vi-command/cancel` widget (lines 4627-4643) is designed to:
1. If in single-command mode: exit single-command mode
2. Otherwise: show a `:q` or `:q!` prompt to exit bash

This is **vim-like behavior**, not bash-like behavior.

**Available widgets for clearing the buffer:**
- `discard-line` (line 7996 of edit.sh) - This is what you want! It clears the buffer, reverts edits, and shows a fresh prompt
- `kill-whole-line` - Kills current line
- `unix-line-discard` - Discards from start to cursor
- `cancel` - Context-dependent cancellation

**Solution for Issue 2:**
Add this binding to your 04_blesh.bash AFTER the C-RET bindings:

```bash
# === Ctrl+C in normal mode: clear buffer instead of showing :q prompt ===
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' 'discard-line'
```

This makes C-c behave like non-vi bash: clear the input and show a fresh prompt. The complete behavior will then be:
- In vi_imap (insert mode): C-c enters normal mode (line 6388, unchanged)
- In vi_nmap (normal mode): C-c clears the buffer via `discard-line` (your new binding)

---

### Summary of Recommended Config Changes

For `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash`, replace lines 47-50 with:

```bash
# vi_imap/nmap: C-RET for intelligent multiline submit
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'

# Alt+Enter fallback (if terminal doesn't emit CSI-u for C-RET)
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'M-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'M-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'

# vi_nmap: C-c clears buffer instead of showing :q prompt
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' 'discard-line'
```

**Key names confirmed:** `C-RET` is correct for CSI-u encoded Ctrl+Enter (your tmux/terminal setup supports this). `S-RET` (Shift+Enter) is NOT reliable for this purpose.

 `./dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash`

```text
1	# 04_blesh.bash - ble.sh-specific tweaks.
2	# Sourced from dot_bashrc.tmpl AFTER ble.sh's --attach=none source but
3	# BEFORE ble-attach (the `bleopt` settings here are read at attach time).
4	# Skipped when ble.sh isn't loaded (no $BLE_VERSION) so plain bash users
5	# don't see errors.
6	
7	[[ -z $BLE_VERSION ]] && return 0
8	
9	# complete_auto_complete = autosuggest mode. 1 = enabled (fish-style ghost
10	# text); empty = disabled. Default to enabled — the whole point of
11	# bringing in ble.sh is the zsh-autosuggestions parity.
12	bleopt complete_auto_complete=1
13	
14	# Hide the message ble.sh prints on attach (attach-greeting), keeps shell
15	# startup quiet.
16	bleopt prompt_eol_mark=
17	
18	# Vi-mode keymap: ble.sh auto-detects `set -o vi` (set in 05_vi_mode.bash)
19	# and activates its full vi-mode. No additional config needed.
20	
21	# Custom keybindings — currently none. Drop ble-bind invocations here
22	# (e.g., `ble-bind -x 'C-r' 'atuin-search-bash'`) when porting zsh
23	# widgets to bash; reminder: anything that was `bindkey -M viins` in zsh
24	# is `ble-bind -m vi_imap -x` in ble.sh.
25	
26	# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter ===
27	#
28	# Default ble.sh + vi-mode behaviour: when the buffer contains a newline
29	# (multi-line paste, multi-line typed input, here-doc etc.), the shell
30	# enters MULTILINE mode and plain RET / Ctrl-M re-binds to "insert
31	# newline" rather than "submit" — meaning Enter alone won't run the
32	# command. The official escape is Ctrl-J (linefeed = accept-line), but
33	# tmux's vim-tmux-navigator already eats `C-j` for pane navigation
34	# (dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:183), so it never reaches ble.sh.
35	#
36	# Ctrl+Enter is the cleanest free key on this stack:
37	#   - tmux extended-keys + xterm:extkeys are enabled, so Ctrl+Enter
38	#     sends a distinct CSI-u sequence (\e[13;5u) which tmux forwards
39	#     intact (no collision with C-j).
40	#   - ble.sh sees `C-RET` as a separate keysym when extended-keys flow
41	#     through, and binds it independently from `RET` / `C-m`.
42	#   - Plain RET still does the safe-multiline-newline thing — useful for
43	#     intentionally building multi-line commands.
44	#
45	# If your terminal can't emit Ctrl+Enter as CSI-u (some minimal SSH
46	# clients), Alt+Enter (`M-RET` below) is a portable fallback.
47	ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
48	ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
49	ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
50	ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
51	
52	# === Suppress mouse keyseq warnings ===
53	#
54	# When ble.sh runs OUTSIDE tmux (e.g. directly in Ghostty / Alacritty), the
55	# terminal forwards mouse-tracking sequences (`ESC[<...M`) into the shell.
56	# ble.sh by default doesn't have a binding for them and warns
57	# `unbind keyseq: mouse` on every mouse click, which cluters the prompt.
58	# Inside tmux mouse events stay in tmux's own copy-mode handler, so the
59	# warning never appears.
60	#
61	# Bind every mouse keyseq variant to `nop` (no-op) — ble.sh swallows the
62	# event silently. Both `xterm` (modern SGR-style) and the legacy `mouse`
63	# pseudo-keysym are covered.
64	ble-bind -f 'mouse' nop 2>/dev/null
65	ble-bind -f 'mouse_xterm' nop 2>/dev/null
66
```

# 05_vi_mode.bash - vi-style command-line editing.
# Sourced from dot_bashrc.tmpl via load_modular_dir "$BASH_CONFIG_DIR" bash.
#
# `set -o vi` enables readline vi mode — modal editing with ESC entering
# normal mode and `i` returning to insert. Less feature-rich than
# zsh-vi-mode (no surround / text-objects beyond readline's basics) but
# adequate for most workflows. ble.sh, when loaded, layers a much more
# zsh-vi-mode-like experience on top — its vi-mode auto-activates if
# ble.sh detects `set -o vi` is set, so this line is the trigger for
# both plain bash and ble.sh paths.

set -o vi

```text
1	# tmux `extended-keys always` corrupts ble.sh paste with `^[[106;5u`
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	Paste a multi-line snippet (e.g. a few diagnostic commands) into a bash
6	shell running under tmux + ble.sh. Instead of the expected:
7	
8	```bash
9	uname -r
10	ldd --version
11	gcc --version
12	```
13	
14	…the prompt buffer shows everything mashed together with `^[[106;5u`
15	between each line:
16	
17	```
18	> uname -r^[[106;5uldd --version^[[106;5ugcc --version^[[106;5upython3 --version^[[106;5ufree -h^[[106;5ulsblk^[[106;5unvidia-smi^[[106;5unumactl --hardware
19	uname: invalid option -- '['
20	ry 'uname --help' for more information.
21	bash: 5uldd: command not found...
22	bash: 5ugcc: command not found...
23	bash: 5upython3: command not found...
24	bash: 5ufree: command not found...
25	bash: 5ulsblkommand not found...
26	bash: 5unvidia-smiommand not found...
27	bash: 5unumactl: command not found...
28	[ble: exit 127]
29	```
30	
31	Each newline in the pasted content shows up as the literal escape
32	sequence `^[[106;5u` (CSI 106;5 u — "Ctrl+J encoded as CSI-u"). bash
33	then runs the whole thing as one mangled command line.
34	
35	## Root cause
36	
37	This repo's tmux config used to set:
38	
39	```tmux
40	set -s extended-keys always
41	```
42	
43	`always` mode forces tmux to re-encode **every** modifier+key combo as
44	CSI-u sequences, including ones that already have legacy encodings.
45	The relevant ones for paste:
46	
47	| Key | Legacy encoding | CSI-u re-encoding under `always` |
48	|-----|----------------|----------------------------------|
49	| `Ctrl+J` | `\n` (LF, 0x0A) | `ESC [ 106 ; 5 u` |
50	| `Ctrl+M` | `\r` (CR, 0x0D) | `ESC [ 109 ; 5 u` |
51	| `Ctrl+I` | `\t` (TAB, 0x09) | `ESC [ 105 ; 5 u` |
52	| `Ctrl+@` | `\0` (NUL) | `ESC [ 64 ; 5 u` |
53	
54	When the user pastes multi-line text, **the terminal sends the embedded
55	`\n` characters as Ctrl+J keystrokes**. tmux's `extended-keys always`
56	catches those and rewrites each one to `ESC[106;5u`. The bracketed-paste
57	markers (`ESC[200~ ... ESC[201~`) wrap the whole thing, but the
58	**inner** content is now a string of mixed visible characters and
59	CSI-u escapes — not the raw `\n` bytes ble.sh's paste handler expects.
60	
61	ble.sh's bracketed-paste handler stuffs the content into the line
62	buffer **as-is**, so the user sees the literal `^[[106;5u` text.
63	
64	The same issue would affect zsh-vi-mode and any other shell with a
65	bracketed-paste handler that doesn't normalize CSI-u back to legacy
66	encodings before insertion.
67	
68	## Fix
69	
70	Change tmux to `on` instead of `always`:
71	
72	```tmux
73	set -s extended-keys on
74	```
75	
76	`on` mode emits CSI-u **only** for keys that have no legacy encoding
77	(Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit, Ctrl+Shift+letter).
78	Standard `Ctrl+letter` keys including `Ctrl+J` keep their legacy
79	single-byte encoding. Paste content stays as raw `\n` and goes into
80	the buffer correctly.
81	
82	The TUIs that needed `extended-keys` in the first place (Claude Code,
83	Neovim, etc.) only ever needed it for the no-legacy-encoding keys
84	(Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/), so they continue to work under `on`.
85	
86	## Verification
87	
88	After applying the fix:
89	
90	```bash
91	tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf   # or open new tmux session
92	```
93	
94	Paste a multi-line snippet. Each line should appear on its own line in
95	the buffer. ble.sh's vi-mode multi-line submit (`Ctrl+Enter` /
96	`Alt+Enter`, see `dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash`) is unaffected.
97	
98	Edge cases that still work under `on`:
99	
100	- `Ctrl+Enter` in Claude Code → still gets CSI-u (no legacy encoding for
101	  that combo)
102	- `Shift+Enter` in Neovim → CSI-u
103	- `Ctrl+1..9` for tmux quick window switching → CSI-u (Ctrl+digit has no
104	  legacy encoding)
105	- `Ctrl+/` in Neovim (comment toggle) → CSI-u (legacy is `Ctrl+_`,
106	  which most TUIs don't decode)
107	- `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` for vim-tmux-navigator → legacy encoding (Ctrl+letter
108	  has clear ASCII bytes 0x08/0x0A/0x0B/0x0C), still works fine
109	
110	## Why we didn't catch this earlier
111	
112	`extended-keys always` was committed back when the repo's primary shell
113	was zsh, and zsh's bracketed-paste handler **does** normalize CSI-u
114	sequences back to their literal characters before buffer insertion (zsh
115	5.9+). The bug only surfaces when:
116	
117	1. Primary shell is bash (`primaryShell=bash` in chezmoi prompt) **or**
118	   ad-hoc bash use is common
119	2. ble.sh is loaded (provides bracketed-paste support, but doesn't
120	   normalize CSI-u → legacy on paste insertion)
121	3. tmux's `extended-keys` is `always` (re-encodes paste-internal
122	   newlines)
123	
124	The combination wasn't tested until a CentOS 7 corporate-server bring-up
125	where the user lived in bash + ble.sh for the bootstrap dance.
126	
127	## Related
128	
129	- [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) —
130	  the one-line fix.
131	- [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) "Key tmux settings for coding agents" —
132	  hard invariant updated to call out the `on` vs `always` distinction.
133	- [`dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash`](../dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash) —
134	  ble.sh + Ctrl+Enter / Alt+Enter accept-line bindings for multi-line
135	  submit (separate concern from this paste-corruption issue).
136	- [`pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`](tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md) —
137	  unrelated CSI-u / extended-keys red herring (display-menu silent
138	  failure was misdiagnosed as a CSI-u issue for hours).
139	- tmux man page: `man tmux` → `extended-keys` (default behaviour and
140	  the difference between `on` / `always`).
141
```

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Compile + install ble.sh into ~/.local/share/blesh after the chezmoi
3	# external clones the source tree (and on subsequent weekly refreshes
4	# whose pull moves HEAD).
5	#
6	# Trigger: change in the cloned repo's HEAD (commit-hash bump). chezmoi's
7	# `include` template function reads the file at template-render time; we
8	# hash the blesh-source HEAD file. NOTE: must be a stable path inside
9	# the repo clone — if the path changes, this script becomes a no-op
10	# until manual `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals`.
11	#
12	# blesh source HEAD: {{ $bleshHead := joinPath .chezmoi.homeDir ".local/share/blesh/.git/HEAD" -}}
13	# {{ if stat $bleshHead -}}{{ include $bleshHead | sha256sum }}{{ else }}absent{{ end }}
14	#
15	# The `make install` target compiles the runtime ble.sh artefact
16	# (~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh) — distinct from the source tree at
17	# ~/.local/share/blesh/. dot_bashrc.tmpl sources the runtime artefact;
18	# without this script, the source clone exists but the runtime doesn't,
19	# and bashrc's presence-gate skips ble.sh init.
20	
21	set -e
22	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
23	
24	info() { echo -e "\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m $1"; }
25	success() { echo -e "\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m $1"; }
26	warn() { echo -e "\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m $1"; }
27	
28	BLESH_SRC="$HOME/.local/share/blesh"
29	
30	if [[ ! -d "$BLESH_SRC" ]]; then
31	    info "ble.sh source not cloned yet (skip — chezmoi external may be in-flight)"
32	    exit 0
33	fi
34	
35	if ! command -v make >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36	    warn "make not found; cannot compile ble.sh. Bash will fall back to plain readline."
37	    warn "Install make (apt-get install build-essential / xcode-select --install) and re-apply."
38	    exit 0
39	fi
40	
41	# ble.sh's Makefile requires GNU awk specifically (not BSD awk on macOS,
42	# not mawk on minimal Ubuntu containers). The bash ansible role installs
43	# `gawk` on every OS; if this script runs before the role (first apply
44	# bootstrap), gracefully no-op so the rest of the apply continues.
45	if ! command -v gawk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
46	    warn "gawk not found; cannot compile ble.sh (Makefile hard-requires GNU awk)."
47	    warn "On Linux: apt-get install gawk / yum install gawk."
48	    warn "On macOS: brew install gawk."
49	    warn "Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after gawk is available."
50	    exit 0
51	fi
52	
53	# Bash 4.0+ check — ble.sh refuses to attach on bash 3.2 (macOS system bash).
54	# On a zsh-primary mac without `brew install bash`, the bash role's brew bash
55	# install is gated on primaryShell == "bash", so the system bash 3.2 stays
56	# active. ble.sh's compile step itself works fine on 3.2 (it's a Makefile),
57	# but the runtime won't attach. We still compile so the artefact exists for
58	# any user who later switches to brew bash or runs bash 5+ ad-hoc.
59	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
60	if [[ -x /opt/homebrew/bin/bash ]]; then
61	    BASH_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash
62	elif [[ -x /usr/local/bin/bash ]]; then
63	    BASH_BIN=/usr/local/bin/bash
64	else
65	    BASH_BIN=$(command -v bash)
66	fi
67	{{ else -}}
68	BASH_BIN=$(command -v bash)
69	{{ end -}}
70	
71	info "Compiling ble.sh (PREFIX=\$HOME/.local; bash=$BASH_BIN)"
72	if make -C "$BLESH_SRC" install PREFIX="$HOME/.local" \
73	        BASH="$BASH_BIN" \
74	        >/tmp/blesh-install.log 2>&1; then
75	    success "ble.sh installed to ~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh"
76	    rm -f /tmp/blesh-install.log
77	else
78	    warn "ble.sh make install failed — see /tmp/blesh-install.log"
79	    warn "Bash will fall back to plain readline (bashrc presence-gate)."
80	    exit 0
81	fi

## Diagnostic Report: ble.sh Issues in Chezmoi Dotfiles

Based on my thorough search of the repository, here are my findings:

### **Issue 1: Ctrl+Enter Multi-line Command Submit**

**Status:** Configuration is CORRECT; issue likely elsewhere

**Relevant Files and Line Numbers:**

1. **`/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash` (Lines 26-50)**
   ```
   Lines 26-43: Documentation explaining multi-line submit strategy
   Line 47: ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
   Line 48: ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
   Line 49: ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
   Line 50: ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'M-RET' accept-line
   ```

2. **`/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf` (Lines 131-151)**
   - **Line 148:** `set -s extended-keys on` ✓ CORRECT (not `always`)
   - **Line 149-150:** Extended-keys-format conditional for tmux 3.5+
   - **Line 151:** `set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'`

3. **`/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_bashrc.tmpl` (Lines 41-53)**
   ```
   Line 50-52: ble.sh source with --attach=none flag
   Line 132-133: ble-attach called at the end
   ```

**Diagnosis:** The `C-RET` (Ctrl+Enter) binding is correctly configured for both `vi_imap` (insert mode) and `vi_nmap` (normal mode) to use `accept-line`. The tmux config correctly uses `extended-keys on` (not `always`), which ensures Ctrl+Enter transmits as a CSI-u sequence while preserving legacy encodings for other keys. 

**Why it might not work:**
- Terminal may not support CSI-u encoding (check: `echo $TERM` in tmux)
- tmux needs to be reloaded: `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf`
- ble.sh may not have re-attached after config changes
- Buffer may not actually contain newlines (test: paste multi-line text, then Ctrl+Enter)

---

### **Issue 2: Ctrl+C in Vi Insert Mode Behavior**

**Status:** NO EXPLICIT BINDING FOUND; using ble.sh defaults

**Critical Finding:** There is NO custom `ble-bind` for Ctrl+C (or `C-c` variant) anywhere in the repository.

**Search Results:**
- Only 8 `ble-bind` calls exist, all in `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash` (Lines 47-65):
  - Lines 47-50: `C-RET` and `M-RET` for accept-line (vi_imap/vi_nmap)
  - Lines 64-65: `mouse` and `mouse_xterm` bound to `nop`

**Diagnosis:** The `:q` prompt on Ctrl+C in vi insert mode is ble.sh's **default behavior**, not something configured in your dotfiles. This is a ble.sh library choice, not a custom keybinding conflict.

```text
  ble/keymap:vi/adjust-command-mode

}
function ble/widget/vi-command/cancel {
  if [[ $_ble_keymap_vi_single_command ]]; then
    _ble_keymap_vi_single_command=
    _ble_keymap_vi_single_command_overwrite=
    ble/keymap:vi/update-mode-indicator
  else
    local joblist; ble/util/joblist
    if ((${#joblist[*]})); then
      ble/array#push joblist $'Type  \e[35m:q!\e[m  and press \e[35m<Enter>\e[m to abandon all \e[31mjobs\e[m and exit Bash'
      IFS=$'\n' builtin eval 'ble/edit/info/show ansi "${joblist[*]}"'
    else
      ble/edit/info/show ansi $'Type  \e[35m:q\e[m  and press \e[35m<Enter>\e[m to exit Bash'
    fi
  fi
  ble/widget/vi-command/bell
  return 0

#!/bin/bash
#%$> out/ble.sh
#%[release = 0]
#%[measure_load_time = 0]
#%[debug_keylogger = 1]
#%[leakvar = ""]
#%#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#%if measure_load_time
_ble_init_measure_prev=
_ble_init_measure_section=
function ble/init/measure/section {
  local now=${EPOCHREALTIME:-$(date +'%s.%N')}

  local s=${now%%[!0-9]*} u=000000
  if [[ $s != "$now" ]]; then
    u=${now##*[!0-9]}000000
    u=${u::6}
  fi
  local stime=$s.$u time=$((s*1000000+10#0$u))

## ble.sh Issues: Debugging Report

I've thoroughly analyzed your ble.sh installation (version 0.4.0-devel4+b99cadb) and found answers to both issues.

### Issue 1: C-RET in Multiline Mode

**The problem:** `C-RET` is bound to `accept-line` in both `vi_imap` and `vi_nmap`, but when there are newlines in the buffer (multiline mode), it doesn't submit.

**Root cause:** This is **expected behavior by design**. When ble.sh detects multiple lines in the buffer (via `ble-edit/content/is-single-line` check), it uses a different widget dispatch:

- In **vi_imap**: RET/C-m is bound to `accept-single-line-or-newline` (which inserts a newline if multiline is detected)
- In **vi_nmap**: RET/C-m is bound to `accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space`

Your current bindings at `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash:47-48`:
```bash
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
```

are using the raw `accept-line` widget which **bypasses the multiline check**. The problem is that you're **not using the `accept-single-line-or` wrapper** that checks if the buffer is multiline first.

**Solution for Issue 1:**
Replace your bindings with the properly conditional version:

```bash
# vi_imap: Use accept-single-line-or-newline for intelligent newline/submit behavior
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'

# vi_nmap: Use accept-single-line-or wrapper for intelligent behavior
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'
```

Alternatively, if you want C-RET to **always submit** (even in multiline mode), keep your current `accept-line` binding, but understand this means RET will only insert newlines and C-RET will always submit. The current default behavior in vi_imap is:
- RET = smart (insert newline in multiline, submit if complete)
- C-j = always submit (hardcoded in lines 6354-6355 of keymap.vi.sh)

**Key insight:** There is NO separate `multiline_imap` or `multiline_nmap` keymap. ble.sh uses conditional widget dispatch (`accept-single-line-or` wrapper) instead of separate keymaps to handle multiline detection.

---

### Issue 2: C-c in Vi Normal Mode Shows `:q` Instead of Clearing Buffer

**Current behavior:** When you press Ctrl+C in vi insert mode, it correctly exits to normal mode. But in normal mode, Ctrl+C shows a `:q` prompt instead of clearing the buffer like non-vi mode does.

**Root cause:** The binding at line 4754 of `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/blesh/lib/keymap.vi.sh`:
```bash
ble-bind -f 'C-c' vi-command/cancel
```

The `vi-command/cancel` widget (lines 4627-4643) is designed to:
1. If in single-command mode: exit single-command mode
2. Otherwise: show a `:q` or `:q!` prompt to exit bash

This is **vim-like behavior**, not bash-like behavior.

**Available widgets for clearing the buffer:**
- `discard-line` (line 7996 of edit.sh) - This is what you want! It clears the buffer, reverts edits, and shows a fresh prompt
- `kill-whole-line` - Kills current line
- `unix-line-discard` - Discards from start to cursor
- `cancel` - Context-dependent cancellation

**Solution for Issue 2:**
Add this binding to your 04_blesh.bash AFTER the C-RET bindings:

```bash
# === Ctrl+C in normal mode: clear buffer instead of showing :q prompt ===
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' 'discard-line'
```

This makes C-c behave like non-vi bash: clear the input and show a fresh prompt. The complete behavior will then be:
- In vi_imap (insert mode): C-c enters normal mode (line 6388, unchanged)
- In vi_nmap (normal mode): C-c clears the buffer via `discard-line` (your new binding)

---

### Summary of Recommended Config Changes

For `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash`, replace lines 47-50 with:

```bash
# vi_imap/nmap: C-RET for intelligent multiline submit
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'

# Alt+Enter fallback (if terminal doesn't emit CSI-u for C-RET)
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'M-RET' 'accept-single-line-or-newline'
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'M-RET' 'accept-single-line-or vi-command/forward-first-non-space'

# vi_nmap: C-c clears buffer instead of showing :q prompt
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' 'discard-line'
```

**Key names confirmed:** `C-RET` is correct for CSI-u encoded Ctrl+Enter (your tmux/terminal setup supports this). `S-RET` (Shift+Enter) is NOT reliable for this purpose.

# Plan: Fix ble.sh multiline submit and Ctrl+C discard

## Context

Two usability issues reported with ble.sh in bash vi-mode:

1. **Ctrl+Enter doesn't submit multi-line commands** — The binding `C-RET → accept-line` exists in `vi_imap`/`vi_nmap`, but multi-line pastes stay stuck. The most likely cause: the terminal or tmux is not forwarding the CSI-u sequence `\e[13;5u` to ble.sh in a way it decodes to the named keysym `C-RET`. Since `accept-line` *bypasses* the multiline check (submits unconditionally), the logic is correct — the key just isn't arriving.

2. **Ctrl+C in vi-mode shows `:q` prompt** — ble.sh default bindings (line 6388 of `keymap.vi.sh`): insert-mode C-c calls `vi_imap/normal-mode-without-insert-leave` (enters normal mode); normal-mode C-c (line 4754) calls `vi-command/cancel` which displays the vim-style `:q` dialog. The user wants normal-mode C-c to discard the buffer and return a fresh prompt (bash/zsh muscle memory).

## Critical files

- `dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash` — the only file to edit
- `~/.local/share/blesh/lib/keymap.vi.sh` — ble.sh source reference (read-only, no edit)

## Implementation

### Change 1 — Multiline submit: add S-RET + raw CSI-u fallbacks

Keep the existing `C-RET` bindings. Add:
- **`S-RET` (Shift+Enter)** bindings — the user asked whether this is better. Ghostty + tmux `extended-keys on` forwards `\e[13;2u`; it is generally more reliably emitted than `\e[13;5u` by terminal emulators.
- **Raw escape sequence fallbacks** — `$'\e[13;5u'` (C-RET in CSI-u) and `$'\e[13;2u'` (S-RET in CSI-u). These match even if ble.sh's named-keysym decoder doesn't map the sequence to `C-RET`/`S-RET`.

Widget stays `accept-line` (not `accept-single-line-or-newline` — that would *insert* a newline in multiline mode, which is the opposite of what we want).

Replace the existing multiline-submit block (lines 26–50) with:

\```bash
# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter ===
#
# In ble.sh vi-mode, plain RET in multiline buffers inserts a newline
# (safe default). We want Ctrl+Enter OR Shift+Enter to always submit.
# accept-line bypasses the single-line check — correct for an explicit
# "submit now" key.
#
# Key encoding path:
#   Terminal emits CSI-u: \e[13;5u (C-RET) or \e[13;2u (S-RET)
#   tmux forwards via extended-keys on + terminal-features xterm*:extkeys
#   ble.sh decodes to named keysym C-RET / S-RET
#
# We bind both the named keysyms (-f flag) AND the raw escape sequences
# as belt-and-suspenders in case the decoder chain drops a link.
#
# Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter collisions: none on this stack.
# tmux C-j (vim-tmux-navigator) eats plain C-j; C-RET and S-RET use
# distinct CSI-u codes that tmux forwards intact.
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'S-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'S-RET' accept-line
# Raw CSI-u fallbacks (belt and suspenders)
ble-bind -m vi_imap $'\e[13;5u' accept-line  # C-RET raw
ble-bind -m vi_nmap $'\e[13;5u' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_imap $'\e[13;2u' accept-line  # S-RET raw
ble-bind -m vi_nmap $'\e[13;2u' accept-line
\```

Remove the `M-RET` fallback lines (49–50) — Alt+Enter is only needed for terminals that can't emit CSI-u at all; S-RET raw covers that use-case better and doesn't risk colliding with future Alt-key widgets.

### Change 2 — Ctrl+C in normal mode: discard instead of `:q`

Add a new section after the mouse-nop block:

\```bash
# === Ctrl+C in vi normal mode: discard buffer (bash muscle memory) ===
#
# Default vi_nmap C-c calls vi-command/cancel which shows a vim-style
# :q / :q! prompt. Muscle memory from bash / zsh expects C-c to clear
# the buffer and return a fresh prompt.
#
# Behaviour after this binding:
#   Insert mode  C-c  → enter normal mode   (ble.sh default, unchanged)
#   Normal mode  C-c  → discard-line        (clear buffer, fresh prompt)
#
# Two C-c presses from insert mode clear the line; one C-c from normal
# mode clears immediately.
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' discard-line
\```

## Verification

After `chezmoi apply` and opening a fresh bash session:

1. **Multiline Shift+Enter**: paste or type a multi-line block (use `<RET>` between lines), then press Shift+Enter → command should submit.
2. **Multiline Ctrl+Enter**: same test; if terminal forwards CSI-u, Ctrl+Enter also submits.
3. **Single-line Enter**: plain Enter still submits single-line commands (unchanged widget).
4. **Ctrl+C insert mode**: start typing, press C-c → goes to normal mode, buffer still visible.
5. **Ctrl+C normal mode**: from normal mode, press C-c → buffer cleared, fresh prompt (no :q dialog).
6. **Ctrl+C twice from insert**: start typing, press C-c, C-c → buffer cleared.
7. **Confirm binding active**: run `ble-bind -P | grep -E 'RET|C-c'` in a bash session to see effective bindings.

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Fix ble.sh multiline submit and Ctrl+C discard

## Context

Two usability issues reported with ble.sh in bash vi-mode:

1. **Ctrl+Enter doesn't submit multi-line commands** — The binding `C-RET → accept-line` exists in `vi_imap`/`vi_nmap`, but multi-line pastes stay stuck. The most likely cause: the terminal or tmux is not forwarding the CSI-u sequence `\e[13;5u` to ble.sh in a way it decodes to the named keysym `C-RET`. Since `accept-line` *bypasses* the multiline check (submits unconditionally), the logic is correct — the key just isn't arriving.

2. **Ctrl+C in vi-mode shows `:q` prompt** — ble.sh default bindings (line 6388 of `keymap.vi.sh`): insert-mode C-c calls `vi_imap/normal-mode-without-insert-leave` (enters normal mode); normal-mode C-c (line 4754) calls `vi-command/cancel` which displays the vim-style `:q` dialog. The user wants normal-mode C-c to discard the buffer and return a fresh prompt (bash/zsh muscle memory).

## Critical files

- `dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash` — the only file to edit
- `~/.local/share/blesh/lib/keymap.vi.sh` — ble.sh source reference (read-only, no edit)

## Implementation

### Change 1 — Multiline submit: add S-RET + raw CSI-u fallbacks

Keep the existing `C-RET` bindings. Add:
- **`S-RET` (Shift+Enter)** bindings — the user asked whether this is better. Ghostty + tmux `extended-keys on` forwards `\e[13;2u`; it is generally more reliably emitted than `\e[13;5u` by terminal emulators.
- **Raw escape sequence fallbacks** — `$'\e[13;5u'` (C-RET in CSI-u) and `$'\e[13;2u'` (S-RET in CSI-u). These match even if ble.sh's named-keysym decoder doesn't map the sequence to `C-RET`/`S-RET`.

Widget stays `accept-line` (not `accept-single-line-or-newline` — that would *insert* a newline in multiline mode, which is the opposite of what we want).

Replace the existing multiline-submit block (lines 26–50) with:

```bash
# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter ===
#
# In ble.sh vi-mode, plain RET in multiline buffers inserts a newline
# (safe default). We want Ctrl+Enter OR Shift+Enter to always submit.
# accept-line bypasses the single-line check — correct for an explicit
# "submit now" key.
#
# Key encoding path:
#   Terminal emits CSI-u: \e[13;5u (C-RET) or \e[13;2u (S-RET)
#   tmux forwards via extended-keys on + terminal-features xterm*:extkeys
#   ble.sh decodes to named keysym C-RET / S-RET
#
# We bind both the named keysyms (-f flag) AND the raw escape sequences
# as belt-and-suspenders in case the decoder chain drops a link.
#
# Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter collisions: none on this stack.
# tmux C-j (vim-tmux-navigator) eats plain C-j; C-RET and S-RET use
# distinct CSI-u codes that tmux forwards intact.
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'S-RET' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'S-RET' accept-line
# Raw CSI-u fallbacks (belt and suspenders)
ble-bind -m vi_imap $'\e[13;5u' accept-line  # C-RET raw
ble-bind -m vi_nmap $'\e[13;5u' accept-line
ble-bind -m vi_imap $'\e[13;2u' accept-line  # S-RET raw
ble-bind -m vi_nmap $'\e[13;2u' accept-line
```

Remove the `M-RET` fallback lines (49–50) — Alt+Enter is only needed for terminals that can't emit CSI-u at all; S-RET raw covers that use-case better and doesn't risk colliding with future Alt-key widgets.

### Change 2 — Ctrl+C in both vi maps: discard like zsh

Desired behaviour (matches zsh insert-mode C-c):
- Typed text stays visible in the terminal scroll buffer (can copy it)
- `^C` marker appears on the line
- A fresh prompt is shown immediately
- **No normal-mode transition** — Escape still handles that

ble.sh default bindings being overridden:
- `vi_imap C-c` → `vi_imap/normal-mode-without-insert-leave` (enters normal mode) — override to `discard-line`
- `vi_nmap C-c` → `vi-command/cancel` (shows `:q` dialog) — override to `discard-line`

Add a new section after the mouse-nop block:

```bash
# === Ctrl+C: discard buffer (zsh / bash muscle memory) ===
#
# ble.sh vi-mode defaults:
#   vi_imap C-c → enter normal mode (vi behaviour)
#   vi_nmap C-c → vi-command/cancel (:q prompt)
#
# Desired: match zsh insert-mode C-c — cancel the line, keep old text
# visible in the scroll buffer (can still copy it), show a fresh prompt.
# Escape still transitions insert → normal mode as expected by vi muscle
# memory; C-c is now unconditionally "cancel and new prompt" from either
# mode.
ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-c' discard-line
ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-c' discard-line
```

## Verification

After `chezmoi apply` and opening a fresh bash session:

1. **Multiline Shift+Enter**: paste or type a multi-line block (use `<RET>` between lines in insert mode), then press Shift+Enter → command submits.
2. **Multiline Ctrl+Enter**: same test; should also submit if terminal forwards CSI-u.
3. **Single-line Enter**: plain Enter still submits (unchanged widget).
4. **C-c from insert mode**: type something, press C-c → old text visible above, fresh prompt (no mode transition).
5. **C-c from normal mode** (entered via Escape): press Escape then C-c → same cancel behaviour.
6. **Escape still works for normal mode**: press Escape while typing → enters normal mode as usual.
7. **Confirm bindings active**: `ble-bind -P | grep -E 'RET|C-c'` in a live bash session.
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-05-07 15:01:00Z)**_

Ghostty/cmux 不需要加。Ghostty 原生支援 kitty keyboard protocol（CSI-u），Ctrl+Enter 和 Shift+Enter 的 `\e[13;5u` / `\e[13;2u` 序列是**自動發出**的，不需要手動設定。

Alacritty 才需要手動加，因為它預設不送 CSI-u for Ctrl+Enter（alacritty.toml 裡那行 comment 也提到了：「Alacritty doesn't natively send CSI-u for Ctrl+Number; Ghostty/cmux does.」）

所以：
- **Ghostty / cmux** — 不動，C-RET binding 在 ble.sh 直接生效 ✓  
- **Alacritty** — 剛剛補了 `Ctrl+Return → \u001b[13;5u` ✓

-# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter ===
+# === Multi-line submit: Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter ===
 #
-# Default ble.sh + vi-mode behaviour: when the buffer contains a newline
-# (multi-line paste, multi-line typed input, here-doc etc.), the shell
-# enters MULTILINE mode and plain RET / Ctrl-M re-binds to "insert
-# newline" rather than "submit" — meaning Enter alone won't run the
-# command. The official escape is Ctrl-J (linefeed = accept-line), but
-# tmux's vim-tmux-navigator already eats `C-j` for pane navigation
-# (dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf:183), so it never reaches ble.sh.
+# In ble.sh vi-mode, plain RET in multiline buffers inserts a newline
+# (safe default). Ctrl+Enter and Shift+Enter always submit via
+# accept-line, which bypasses the single-line check unconditionally.
 #
-# Ctrl+Enter is the cleanest free key on this stack:
-#   - tmux extended-keys + xterm:extkeys are enabled, so Ctrl+Enter
-#     sends a distinct CSI-u sequence (\e[13;5u) which tmux forwards
-#     intact (no collision with C-j).
-#   - ble.sh sees `C-RET` as a separate keysym when extended-keys flow
-#     through, and binds it independently from `RET` / `C-m`.
-#   - Plain RET still does the safe-multiline-newline thing — useful for
-#     intentionally building multi-line commands.
+# Key encoding path:
+#   Terminal emits CSI-u: \e[13;5u (C-RET) or \e[13;2u (S-RET)
+#   tmux forwards via: extended-keys on + terminal-features xterm*:extkeys
+#   ble.sh decodes to named keysym C-RET / S-RET
 #
-# If your terminal can't emit Ctrl+Enter as CSI-u (some minimal SSH
-# clients), Alt+Enter (`M-RET` below) is a portable fallback.
+# Both the named keysyms (-f flag) AND the raw escape sequences are bound
+# as belt-and-suspenders in case the decode chain drops a link.
+# S-RET (Shift+Enter) tends to be more reliably emitted by terminal
+# emulators than C-RET, so both are offered.
+#
+# Collision check: tmux C-j (vim-tmux-navigator pane nav) eats plain
+# C-j; C-RET and S-RET use distinct CSI-u codes that tmux forwards intact.
 ble-bind -m vi_imap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
 ble-bind -m vi_nmap -f 'C-RET' accept-line
